# Repeated Substring Pattern.

@example Blocks of three letters give "dog" three times.
"dogdogdog"
=> true

@example With 5 letters the only blocks possible are single letters, and they differ. "xyz" does start over, but its second copy is cut short.
"xyzxy"
=> false

@example The blocks of two are "no" and "on": the same letters, in another order.
"noon"
=> false

# A single letter is only one block.
"a"
=> false

# Two different letters.
"ab"
=> false

# One letter throughout, with a prime length.
"zzzzzzz"
=> true

# Three copies: the two halves of s differ, but blocks of 2 work.
"xyxyxy"
=> true

# Five copies of a three-letter block.
"pqrpqrpqrpqrpqr"
=> true

# The block is itself a repetition: blocks of 2 and of 4 both work.
"cdcdcdcd"
=> true

# The first and last blocks of 3 are equal, but the middle one isn't.
"abcxyzabc"
=> false

# Every block of 3 has the letters a, b, c, in a different order each time.
"abcbcacab"
=> false

# The block's first letter comes back inside it: trying only the shortest
# block length, or only the block that ends where s[0] first comes back,
# gives the wrong answer.
"aabaab"
=> true

"abacabac"
=> true

# Only the last letter breaks the pattern.
"xyxyxyxyxz"
=> false

# 719 letters a and a final b: 720 has 29 block lengths to try, and each
# fails only at the last block.
""
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 6 small
"abaabaabaab"
=> false

@gen 9 small
"abababa"
=> false

@gen 11 small
"bbabbabaa"
=> false

@gen 13 small
"bbaabbaa"
=> true

@gen 17 small
"babbabbabbab"
=> true

@gen 21 small
"babbbabbbabb"
=> true

@gen 23 small
"aacbac"
=> false

@gen 25 small
"acaacaacaac"
=> false

# A full-size random case: 10^4 letters, a block of 1250 written 8 times.
# s + s needs 2 * 10^4 letters here, plus the closing NUL.
@gen 10
""
=> true
